source.summary: GitHub Actions 'Embedder footprint' runs for PR #252 (branch fix/170-parse-nesting-complexity at commit eebf876bce0385f3ac556d0051a577b6d8958c77, the merge of the PR head f816ff188c499161530081913ee69d10ad20f1c3 with main 07f9a49120bf4d465c1704692a496f4e2f108bb0; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45054630647 and 45054643208 against the branch and pull-request run 45054539493, which built the same merge tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #252 (#170, parse time grows cubically with block nesting). The PR rewrites two optimizer analysis passes in crates/telomere/src/parser/core/optimizer/pipeline/analysis.rs: compute_loop_depth becomes a dominator-tree prefix sum accumulated in one reverse-postorder pass, and compute_loop_parents is inverted from an all-pairs scan to a single pass over each loop's members; the PR's only other change is a criterion bench, which is not linked into the embedder. The parser/optimizer is part of the telomere library linked into every embedder configuration except baseline, so the deltas are nearly uniform across library configurations and the baseline configuration is unchanged: in the release profile the library configurations shrink slightly (stripped .text -224 B in all six; stripped file -72 B, wasi-threads -88 B, component -56 B), while in the release-size profile (opt-level "z", fat LTO, one codegen unit) they grow (stripped file +1,120 B and stripped .text +960 B, with core-nosimd and core-jit at +1,104 B / +944 B). 24 of 28 gated series changed; the 4 unchanged series are the baseline configuration's. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, 'Size regression gate (#164)'.
